Round 61 verification: **PASS**. I found no bugs. Every browser check in the task ran and passed at 1440├ù900 and 1280├ù720, and I changed no app source.

**The fixes A made, checked in a real browser:**
- **Pressing an empty part of the open menu (C-R60-01):** I pressed the menu's padding with the left, right and middle buttons, and its divider line with left and right. Each time, focus stayed on the current menu item, ArrowDown moved down, and Escape closed the menu. The right press still showed no browser menu.
- **Holding a key while clicking outside the menu (C-R60-02):** with Shift already held, the click that closes the menu did nothing (Snap stayed off). The next normal click turned Snap on. The page did receive the repeated key press, so this is a real test of the fix.
- **Scrolling up/down with the menu open during playback (ROOT-R50-58-L1):** scrolling the tracks closed the menu at both sizes. Playback kept going, Follow stayed on, and the horizontal position didn't move.
- **Extra check I added:** I also ran Follow with the tracks enlarged so they overflow vertically. When Follow turns the page, the menu stays open and the vertical position doesn't change, so the new scroll-close rule doesn't break that case.
- **Earlier behaviour still works:**
  - clicking an item, including on its text;
  - the menu keys, and Space in the menu choosing without starting playback;
  - a click on Snap, Play or Export that closes the menu does nothing else, and the next click works;
  - a key pressed while the mouse is still held still works;
  - the menu stays open across a Follow page flip;
  - number keys on the division select.

**Code checks:**
- The type check, all 1556 tests and the build pass, and `npm run verify` passed on the first try. Biome shows the same 5 known line-ending errors as before.
- The source changes are only the ones the task allowed, the 35 existing menu tests are unchanged, and all other files match the frozen and protected lists.
- **Deliberate-bug tests:** each bug I put into a scratch copy was caught by the test meant to catch it. Three survived:
  - a 2 px scroll tolerance, which the task expected to survive;
  - dropping the line that removes the key listener, which only a code read catches;
  - checking for the button element itself instead of anything inside it, which unit tests miss but the real browser test of clicking the item's text covers.

**Login protection is not bypassed:**
- In a fresh browser with no login, `/studio-lab` opens the demo with the "no sign-in needed" badge.
- No requests went to the token, recording, download or file-storage addresses, and none carried a login header.
- `/studio/middle-east` asks you to sign in.
- A token request without a login gets 401.
- A token request with a fake login got 403 yesterday. Today it got 500 because the backend was down, but access is still refused.

**Things you should know:**
- **Backend down:** after the machine restart, the backend on :5199 was down for this whole session. I ran the browser checks anyway because the demo page only asks it for the cart. B can discount those runs; restarting the backend before the next round would remove the doubt.
- **Browser tool restart:** the browsing tool restarted itself once during a 1440 run, which reset the page. I re-ran that check once and it passed.
- **Not tested:** these can't be tested in a headless browser and go to the Tech Lead's manual list:
  - real key-repeat timing;
  - a real Alt-Tab while holding the mouse;
  - the select's native popup with keys;
  - Ctrl/Cmd plus a number.
- **Out of scope:** video sync, the full find ΓåÆ add ΓåÆ fit video ΓåÆ export flow with WAV checks, and the FB-01..FB-16 regression were outside this round's scope, so none of them is claimed as passed.
- **Ableton:** the grid width in the track menu matches Ableton's manual. For the other three behaviours there is no Ableton source, so they are recorded as unconfirmed.

**Commit readiness for root:** round 61, round 60, round 59 and the rounds 50ΓÇô58 bundle are each ready as an interim checkpoint, not a release. B's follow-up list includes the earlier open items from the root review and the publication checkpoint.
